entities.name: PMID:25424888
observations: Secondary longitudinal analysis of the Welfare, Children & Families: A Three City Study in 835 low-income ethnic-minority mother-child pairs; children were birth to 4 years at baseline, with 41% African-American and 59% Latina mothers.
Maternal television-content regulation at wave 1 was categorized as high (71%), some (21%), or none (8%); child total television viewing was measured about 16 months later.
No maternal content regulation predicted 0.91 more units of child television viewing than high regulation at follow-up (β=0.91, 95% CI 0.09–1.73), supporting less viewing with greater regulation.

entities.name: Maternal TV regulation
observations: In a low-income African-American and Latina sample, children of mothers reporting no regulation of television content watched significantly more television at follow-up than children of high-regulation mothers (β=0.91, 95% CI 0.09–1.73).
